title: Shark Attacks
text:
The Global Shark Attack File (GSAF) is a long-running collection of reported shark-human incidents. It records details such as where and when incidents occurred, what people were doing, and the reported outcome. These records are useful for exploring patterns, but they do not capture every encounter or measure a person’s risk.
Shark attacks are rare compared with the many people who spend time in the ocean, and fatal attacks are rarer still. Dramatic stories can make the danger feel more common than it is; incident counts alone also cannot tell us the risk per swim or surf session.
Use the Map page to explore recorded attacks by country, and the Trends page to compare fatal and non-fatal incidents across activities.
